title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 17
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 17: a dry morsel with quietness, friendship, and the cheerful heart.

questions.text: What does this chapter say is better than a house full of feasting with strife?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:1 says better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

answers.text: A dinner of herbs with love

questions.text: The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold, but what does Yahweh test?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:3 says the refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but Yahweh tests the hearts.

questions.text: What does this chapter call the crown of old men?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:6 says children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their parents.

questions.text: What does he who covers an offense promote?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:9 says he who covers an offense promotes love, but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.

questions.text: According to this chapter, what is it better to meet than a fool in his folly?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:12 says let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

answers.text: A bear robbed of her cubs

questions.text: What is the beginning of strife compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:14 says the beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.

questions.text: When does a friend love, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 says a friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

questions.text: What does a cheerful heart make, according to this saying?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:22 says a cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

questions.text: Where do the eyes of a fool wander, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:24 says wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

answers.text: To the ends of the earth

questions.text: According to the last verse, how is even a fool counted when he keeps silent?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:28 says even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise; when he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
